question.problem:
An unfair coin has a $20%$ chance of landing on heads. The coin is tossed $10$ times. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, what is the probability of getting heads at least $3$ times?

Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times the coin landed on heads.

Here, we have the following information:

- There are $n=10$ tosses.

- The probability of landing on heads is $p=20%=0.2.$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(10,0.2).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for the probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.2)^{x}(1-0.2)^{10-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.2)^{x}(0.8)^{10-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability of getting heads at least $3$ times. This corresponds to $P(X\ge 3).$

However, computing

$$
P(X\ge 3)=P(X=3)+P(X=4)+…+P(X=10)
$$

will involve many computations, so let's express our answer in terms of the complement instead. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & =1-[P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2)] \\  & =1-[(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{0})(0.2)^{0}(0.8)^{10-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{1})(0.2)^{1}(0.8)^{10-1} \\  & \,\,+\,(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{2})(0.2)^{2}(0.8)^{10-2}] \\  & =1-[(0.8)^{10}+10(0.2)(0.8)^{9}+45(0.2)^{2}(0.8)^{8}] \\  & ≈1-0.677\,800 \\  & ≈0.322,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
